own_solution.law: Newton's second law along the incline (or work-energy theorem): a = g(sin theta - mu_k cos theta); v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a d
assumptions: block treated as a particle sliding without tipping
block starts from rest at the start of the 4 m
block does start to slide (mu_s < tan 30 deg = 0.577)

T4340.regime: mu_s < tan(30 deg) = 0.577 so the block starts sliding from rest; 0.35 is inside this regime

T1BB6.regime: mu_s < tan(30 deg) = 0.577 so the block starts sliding from rest; 0.35 is inside this regime

notes: a = 9.8(0.5 - 0.15*0.8660) = 3.627 m/s^2; v = sqrt(2*3.627*4) = 5.387 m/s. With the 2 m prior slide on the same incline, v0^2 = 2*3.627*2 = 14.51, v^2 = 43.52, v = 6.597 m/s. Mass variants (T9630, T8540) both state 2 kg; static-friction variants (T4340, T1BB6) both state 0.35; prior-slide variants (TD05D, T908A, T4D96, T1D64) all state 2 m. TD05D/T1D64 slightly strain the base wording 'released from rest ... slides 4 m' but each explicitly says the stated distance began after 2 m of sliding, so the reading is unambiguous. T908A/T4D96 imply the block was placed on the incline and then released from rest, so the earlier slide is disconnected.
